transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because... things have been pretty stressful at my job lately. I'm a transportation inspector, and ever since I won this county safety award a while back, certain people at work have been coming after me. 

They've been twisting my inspection reports around, and they keep asking these really pointed budget questions. It's like they're trying to make me look crooked. I brought it up to my supervisor, and he says it’s just a normal review process, but... I mean, I can tell what's actually going on. There's definitely a coordinated effort to discredit me.

When your supervisor told you this was just a normal review process, did that explanation make sense to you at all, or are you completely certain that he's either mistaken or part of what's happening?

No, it didn't make sense to me at all. I mean, I know what a normal review looks like, and this isn't it. I'm completely certain about what I'm seeing. Ever since I got that county safety award, it's just been one thing after another. They take my inspection reports and they twist the wording around, and then they come at me with these really specific budget questions... it's all designed to make me look like I'm doing something crooked. So when my supervisor says it's just a normal review, he's either completely blind to it or he's in on it. I can just tell there is a coordinated effort going on to discredit me.
Before you won the county safety award, did you ever have concerns that people at work were trying to undermine you or act against you in some way?

No, not before the award. Before that, everything was fine. It's really just been going on for about a year now... right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That's when all this started.
Is there any possibility at all, even a small one, that your supervisor might actually be telling you the truth and this really is just a standard review process?

No, there's no possibility. I mean, I've been doing this job for a while, and I know how a standard review works. This isn't it. Like I said, it all started right after that county safety award. That's when they started twisting my inspection reports and asking those really pointed budget questions. It's obvious they're trying to make me look crooked. So when my supervisor says it's just a normal review... well, he's just wrong. I can clearly tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me.

Apart from what's happening at work with these people trying to discredit you, how are things going in other areas of your life—your personal relationships, your home situation, your hobbies or interests?

Honestly, everything else is fine. I still get to work on time every day, I complete my inspections... I take care of myself and keep up with church, stuff like that. My personal life is pretty normal. The main problems really only come up when people bring up those reports or try to question my spending. But outside of that, yeah, things are going alright.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?

No, I've never had anything like that happen. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine. It's just the stuff at work with the reports and the budget that I'm dealing with.

When your supervisor and colleagues ask these budget questions or review your reports, do you think they're doing this specifically because they want to harm you or discredit you, or could there be other explanations—like maybe they're just doing their job but it happens to affect you?

No, I don't think there are other explanations. Like I said before, it all started right after that county safety award. Before that, everything was fine. But since then, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking those really pointed budget questions. It's not just them doing their jobs. They're doing it like they're trying to make me look crooked. Even when my supervisor tries to tell me it's just a normal review, I can tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's too specific to just be a coincidence.

When these colleagues ask you budget questions or review your reports, do you think they're specifically targeting you personally because of who you are, or do you think they might be doing this to multiple people at work for various reasons?

It's definitely just me. I mean, they aren't doing this to the other inspectors. Like I mentioned, it all ties back to when I got that county safety award. Since then, they've been specifically twisting my inspection reports and coming at me with those pointed budget questions. They want to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just a normal review that everyone goes through, but... I know what I'm seeing. It is a coordinated effort to discredit me, personally. They aren't going after anyone else like this.

If I were to tell you that I reviewed your personnel file and the supervisory process you're describing is actually standard practice at your workplace for all inspectors, would you be able to accept that possibility, or would you still be certain that something coordinated is happening against you?

I mean... I hear what you're saying, but no, I wouldn't really be able to accept that. 

Like I've been saying, I know my supervisor claims it's just a normal review process. But I'm the one actually dealing with it every day. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports on purpose. They keep asking these really pointed budget questions because they're trying to make me look crooked. So even if a file says it's standard practice, I can just tell there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's not just regular procedure.
